ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Many people enjoy using the navigation function of their smartphones while driving, which has led to the popularity of a "car magnetic phone mount." As shown in Figure A, the mount's suction cup has a magnetic feature that firmly secures the phone. Figure B is a side-view schematic of the phone attached to the mount (the mount is equivalent to an inclined plane with an angle of $\theta$). If the phone has a mass of $m=200\,\text{g}$, the mount's inclination angle is $\theta=53^{\circ}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the phone and the mount's surface is $\mu=0.3$, and both the phone and the mount are in a stationary state, the maximum static friction between the mount and the phone is approximately equal to the kinetic friction. Given that $\sin53^{\circ}=0.8$, $\cos53^{\circ}=0.6$, and $g=10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Without magnetic attraction, determine whether the phone will slide down through calculation.
2. If the magnetic attraction force between them is $F=6\mathrm{N}$, find the magnitude of the normal force and the frictional force exerted by the bracket on the phone.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, Figure A shows the mobile phone supported by the vehicle-mounted bracket, and next to it there is an arrow labeled “Suction cup”, indicating that the bracket suction cup/magnetic attraction part is in contact with the mobile phone; Figure B is a simplified side-view diagram, drawing the contact surface between the mobile phone and the bracket as an inclined long strip, making an angle θ with the horizontal plane, so the mobile phone has a tendency to slide downward along the inclined plane under the action of gravity. Reasoning: It is known that m=200 g=0.200 kg, g=10 m/s², so the gravity of the mobile phone mg=0.200×10=2 N. θ=53°, sin53°=0.8, cos53°=0.6, and the coefficient of friction μ=0.3. 1. When there is no magnetic force, the supporting force perpendicular to the contact surface is N=mg cosθ=2×0.6=1.2 N. The maximum static friction is approximately f_max=μN=0.3×1.2=0.36 N. The component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sinθ=2×0.8=1.6 N. Because 1.6 N > 0.36 N, the maximum static friction is not enough to balance the downward-sliding component, so the mobile phone will slide downward along the inclined plane. 2. When there is magnetic attraction force F=6 N, according to the method set by the problem, regard the magnetic force as an attractive force perpendicular to the contact surface and pressing the mobile phone toward the bracket. Therefore the normal force N=mg cosθ+F=1.2+6=7.2 N. The mobile phone and the bracket are stationary, and in the direction along the inclined plane the static friction balances the downward-sliding component of gravity, so the magnitude of the friction force f=mg sinθ=1.6 N, and the direction is upward along the inclined plane. Check: At this time the maximum static friction is about μN=0.3×7.2=2.16 N, greater than 1.6 N, so it can remain stationary.
